R0062.title: Illegal Cash-Out
R0062.definition: Converting funds into a more convenient or valuable form through fraudulent transactions, using the extracted funds for illegal or prohibited purposes.
R0062.description: Refers to converting one form of funds into another more usable or valuable form. This typically involves converting non-cash assets such as credit card limits, points, coupons, or virtual currencies into cash. For example, some people may use a credit card to purchase returnable goods and then return them for cash. Others may sell virtual currencies on trading platforms to convert them into cash.
R0062.influence: Cash-out funds with no real transaction backing flow into restricted sectors such as real estate and gambling, disrupting financial order and weakening AML monitoring effectiveness; the platform bears refund and chargeback losses from fraudulent transactions, credit-card cash-outs degrade issuing-bank asset quality and raise non-performing loans, and large-scale cash-outs trigger regulatory penalties, payment-license revocation, and other criminal and compliance risks.

references.title: Tighter Credit Card Fund Controls: Further Crackdown on Illegal Cash-Out

observables: Frequent fake transactions occur between linked buyer and seller accounts, with funds looping back in a closed cycle
Non-cash assets such as credit card limits, points, or virtual currency are cashed out via returns or transfers, with an abnormally high cash-out ratio
Transactions have no real logistics or goods delivery, with orders concentrated in returnable or transferable categories
The same account cluster repeatedly pays by credit card and immediately refunds and withdraws cash within a short window

R0062-001.title: Credit Card / Loan Cash-Out
R0062-001.definition: Exploiting platform mechanisms to cash out credit card limits or shopping loans.
R0062-001.description: Exploiting platform business process vulnerabilities to withdraw shopping loans to a bank card, or colluding between buyers and sellers to fake shipments and extract shopping loan funds.
R0062-001.influence: Credit card limits or shopping-loan funds are fraudulently withdrawn and diverted from consumption purposes, leaving card issuers and the platform with fund losses and non-performing-loan risk; fraudulent refund transactions create platform advance-payment and channel-chargeback costs, and large-scale cash-outs trigger regulatory interviews, payment-channel downgrades, and credit-card compliance penalties.

references.title: Stronger Supervision on Credit Card Fund Use and Cash-Out Violations

observables: Shopping-loan funds are withdrawn to a bank card without being used for actual consumption
Buyer and seller collude on fake shipments to complete a credit-card payment and then refund to extract cash
Credit-card payment orders cluster, with amounts near the credit limit ceiling and rapid refunds following
The same device or account cluster repeatedly cycles through borrowing, withdrawal, and repayment

R0062-002.title: Illegal Points Cash-Out
R0062-002.definition: Obtaining points through illegal means or converting points into cash in violation of terms of service.
R0062-002.description: Illegal points cash-out may include: a) Fabricated transactions: creating fake transactions to earn points, such as using one's own credit card at one's own store, then canceling the transactions while retaining the points. b) Exploiting system vulnerabilities: using loopholes to obtain extra points without actual spending. c) Buying and selling points: purchasing others' points and reselling them at a higher price, or selling goods redeemed with points at full market price.
R0062-002.influence: Causes financial losses and compliance risks for the platform.

references.title: Case Study: Operating a Money Laundering Platform for Cyber Black-Grey Market Merchants

observables: Self-buying and self-selling fake transactions farm points, with transactions canceled afterward while the points are retained
System vulnerabilities are exploited to bulk-obtain points without any spending, with anomalous point-source patterns
Points are concentrated on redeeming fungible discounted goods that are then resold at full price to cash out
Points are abnormally transferred or resold between accounts, with redemption behavior clustering across accounts
